recognize_zh: 周邊血中一個圓形細胞的核被密集深紫色（異染性）顆粒遮蓋，顆粒大小一致並散落到細胞周圍背景，形似嗜鹼性球但核呈圓形不分葉，為循環中的肥大細胞，符合肥大細胞白血病。
features: Single intermediate-sized round cell among red cells
Round, non-lobulated nucleus largely obscured by granules
Dense, uniform dark purple metachromatic cytoplasmic granules
Numerous granules dispersed around the cell, suggesting degranulation or smear disruption
Background red cells with scattered small granular debris; no other leukocytes in field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a circulating cell with a round, non-lobulated nucleus obscured by dense, uniform, dark purple metachromatic granules, with many granules dispersed into the surrounding background. The appearance is that of a mast cell rather than a basophil. In the appropriate context, and if circulating mast cells constitute at least 10% of leukocytes or marrow aspirate mast cells are at least 20%, findings are consistent with mast cell leukemia; confirmation with tryptase, CD117 and CD25 by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry, serum tryptase and KIT D816V testing is recommended.

ddx.vs: Basophils have a lobulated or segmented nucleus and water-soluble granules, and are CD123 and CD203c positive but CD117 negative.
Basophilic blasts are immature with fine chromatin and nucleoli and are tryptase negative or weak, lacking KIT D816V.

ddx.dx: Acute myeloid leukemia with coarse azurophilic granules (e.g. APL)
ddx.vs: Promyelocytes show reddish-purple granules, Auer rods and strong MPO positivity rather than metachromatic toluidine-blue-positive granules.
